Definition: from the same as G2226 and G64; to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare:--take captive, catch.
BiblicalUsage: Zogreo means to take alive, as a prisoner of war is taken — and Jesus turns the word on its head for Peter: 'from henceforth thou shalt catch men.' Paul uses it again for those snared by the devil, who may yet escape and be taken alive by God instead. The same word covers the hunter's catch and the rescue.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ takes men alive not to destroy them but to save them, and that is the only capture that gives life.
